title: Arbitrary separable field extensions lift across square-zero ideals
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be an extension of fields which is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], meaning that every intermediate field finitely generated as a field over $k$ is separably generated over $k$. For every commutative $k$-algebra $D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, and every $k$-algebra homomorphism $g:L\to D/J$, there exists a $k$-algebra homomorphism $f:L\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$, where $q:D\to D/J$ is the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. No algebraicity, finite generation, or characteristic hypothesis is imposed on $L/k$.

source.place: Tag 0322, proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions, characteristic-zero clause (3) and positive-characteristic implication (1) implies (6); formal smoothness is Definition 00TI, definition-formally-smooth.

proof.text: Let $E$ be any intermediate field of $L/k$ finitely generated as a field over $k$. By the definition of separability [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], $E/k$ is separably generated: choose its separating transcendence basis. Apply [lem-sfb-separably-generated-field-h1-zero] to this extension to obtain $H_1(L_{E/k})=0$. This applies to every such $E$, including $E=k$.

source.place: Tag 0320, proof of (3), finitely generated intermediate extensions and their separating transcendence bases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-finite-subfields] to $k\subseteq L$ and the vanishing just obtained for every finitely generated intermediate field. Its conclusion is $H_1(L_{L/k})=0$. This is the passage through cotangent homology in the source; it does not require choosing compatible lifts on the subfields.

source.place: Tag 0320, proof (3), application of Tag 07BQ, lemma-colimits-NL, to the union of finitely generated intermediate fields.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\Omega_{L/k}$ is an $L$-module. Since $L$ is a field, [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective], with $V=\Omega_{L/k}$, shows that this module is projective. No finite-dimensionality of the differential module is needed.

source.place: Tag 031Z, lemma-characterize-formally-smooth-field-extension, proof: vector spaces are free, hence projective; used at the end of Tag 0320 (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] with $A=k$, $B=L$, $N=J$, and the given $D$ and $g$. Its two hypotheses are exactly the homology vanishing of step 2 and the projectivity of step 3. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], the structure map $k\to D$ gives the required algebra structures and its quotient map is the stated $q:D\to D/J$. The cited lifting theorem therefore produces a $k$-algebra map $f:L\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$, as required.

source.place: Tag 031J, proposition-characterize-formally-smooth, (6) implies (1); the field application is Tag 031Z and the final sentence of Tag 0320 (3).

proof_origin.place: Tag 0320, proof of (3), as used in Tag 0322; Tag 031Z and Tag 031J supply the field lifting criterion.
